findings.evidence:
fn customer_label(db: &dyn Db, invoice: &Invoice) -> Result<String, DbError> {
    let customer = db.customer(invoice.customer_id)?;
findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: `monthly_report` calls `customer_label` for each invoice (src/report.rs:26), which runs `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice — about 3 000 queries per report for 800 distinct customers, growing with the month's invoices. Collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them with the existing batch query `db.customers(&ids)` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`, src/db.rs:26), index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>`, and build each label from the map; keep the current error behavior when a customer is missing.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

fn purchase_order(notes: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let pattern = Regex::new(r"PO-\d{4}-\d{4}").expect("a valid pattern");
findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for each invoice (src/report.rs:28) and compiles the same pattern every time — about 3 000 regex compilations per report, growing with the month's invoices, while compiling costs far more than matching one short note. Compile it once: a `static` `std::sync::OnceLock<Regex>` (or `LazyLock`), or build it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass it in.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
